Subject: SecureAudit + BlueMount: integrated evidence gateway proposal & runbook

Hi Maya / BlueMount team —

Thanks for taking the initial call yesterday. I pulled together the starting proposal for a lightweight evidence gateway integration so customers can push SOC2 / pen-test artifacts from SecureAudit into BlueMount for indexed storage and access, with RBAC preserved. High-level goals:

- Minimal customer config: SSO-based connector + scoped token exchange.
- End-to-end audit trail: transfer metadata, checksums, and ingest timestamps.
- Role-based access mapping between SecureAudit and BlueMount.
- Optional auto-redaction step (customer toggle) before persistence.

Camila, copying you for the integration spec and runbook draft. Sergio, can you confirm if partner enablement (pricing / co-sell) needs an internal review before we share an MOU?

Maya — could you confirm the following by Thu EOD?
1) Preferred retention metadata schema (we proposed retention_days + sensitivity_tag)
2) Any constraints on signed URLs vs. direct S3 PUTs from your side
3) Who on SecureAudit will own the initial connector dev (engineer + PM contact)

I attached a short skeleton of the integration spec to this thread for dev alignment.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0118
[Attachment: integration_spec.yaml (text/yaml)]

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SecureAudit + BlueMount: integrated evidence gateway proposal & runbook

Thanks Vanessa — excited about this. A few clarifying questions from engineering and security:

1) SSO: we prefer OIDC with token exchange (we can run an intermediary exchange service). Will Redwood accept subject_id mapping to user.email?
2) Retention schema: retention_days + sensitivity_tag looks fine, but we need a max retention cap per customer in BlueMount policy; can Redwood provide a retention flag in the payload?
3) Signed URLs vs direct upload: preference is signed PUT URLs (short-lived) to avoid cross-cloud egress billing, but we can support server-server transfer if BlueMount provides temporary credentials.

We can own the initial connector work on our side. Assigning Sarah Lee (eng lead) and Ilya (PM) to the thread.

On attachments: can you forward the integration skeleton as a plain YAML blob in the body? Our firewall strips some attachments.

—Maya
Maya Cohen
Director of Integrations, SecureAudit
maya@secureaudit.com

Hi Maya —

Pasting the (requested) core pieces of the integration skeleton inline so firewall-safe: 

--- integration_spec.yaml (excerpt) ---
connector: 
  auth: 
    method: OIDC-token-exchange
    subject_mapping: user.email
  transfer: 
    method: signed_url
    signed_url_ttl: 15m
  metadata: 
    required: [artifact_id, checksum_sha256, retention_days, sensitivity_tag, source_report_id]
  redaction: 
    optional: true
  audit: 
    include: [transfer_ts, transfer_actor, original_filename]
--- end excerpt ---

Notes:
- retention_days will be honored by BlueMount as maximum retention unless the customer sets a lower value. We will include a retention_cap field in the initial payload.
- Signed URL flow: Redwood will request a signed PUT URL from BlueMount via a server-to-server call; SecureAudit will POST artifacts to the signed URL.
- Where auto-redaction is enabled, Redwood will run a lightweight PII filter before generating the signed URL.

Attachment: I uploaded the full draft spec to Drive (link below) and attached a pointer file to the thread.

Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/secureaudit/integration-spec
